entry.label: Evolutionary cybernetics
entry.description: An evolutionary approach to cybernetics concerned with how new levels of control, adaptation and organisation arise.
entry.canonical_definition: A programme investigating how organisation and control emerge and develop through evolutionary processes; the account here follows Principia Cybernetica.

profile.title: Evolutionary cybernetics
profile.summary: Heylighen proposes investigating how control and goal-directed organisation emerge and develop through evolution. His page also advances a broad interdisciplinary philosophy. Its critical account of second-order cybernetics is his interpretation, not a settled history of the field.
profile.canonical_definition: A programme investigating how organisation and control emerge and develop through evolutionary processes; the account here follows Principia Cybernetica.
profile.why_it_matters: Distinguish a research programme and its proposed mechanisms from established consensus.
profile.context_and_lineage: A project-authored account, not evidence of consensus or historical influence.
profile.editorial_note: Paraphrase of attributed authors’ proposals; no endorsement of forecasts or values.
key_distinctions: The page proposes that variation and selection underlie evolutionary phenomena; this broad claim requires argument and domain-specific evidence.
A descriptive selection process does not, by itself, decide whose survival or welfare should count.
common_misreadings: Treating a proposed mechanism or normative commitment as a settled conclusion.
